name: IA aplicada: convierte procesos en servicios para tus clientes
description:
La IA no solo permite ahorrar tiempo y automatizar tareas. También está creando nuevas oportunidades para profesionales, freelancers y agencias que quieren incorporar nuevas soluciones a los servicios que ya ofrecen a sus clientes.

En este encuentro online veremos **cómo identificar procesos con potencial para aplicar IA, transformarlos en soluciones concretas y convertirlos en servicios que puedas ofrecer de forma clara y repetible a diferentes clientes.**

Hablaremos de casos aplicados a marketing, ventas, atención al cliente, operaciones y otras áreas, con ejemplos concretos y un framework práctico para pasar de una necesidad real a una propuesta de servicio.

## Qué veremos

* Dónde están las oportunidades reales para crear servicios con IA.
* Qué puedes ofrecer con IA en áreas como marketing, ventas, atención al cliente y operaciones.
* Cómo detectar problemas y procesos de tus clientes que pueden convertirse en una solución.
* Cómo pasar de una automatización o agente a una oferta concreta y fácil de entender.
* Qué necesitas para empezar sin tener que desarrollar todo desde cero.
* Cómo crear soluciones que puedas adaptar y reutilizar con distintos clientes.
* Errores habituales al crear una oferta basada en IA.
* Un framework práctico: **problema → solución → proceso → cliente → propuesta → delivery.**
* Ejemplos aplicados a prospección B2B, lead scoring, generación de propuestas, onboarding, reporting, contenido, recepción virtual y otras aplicaciones.

🎓 **Encuentro online gratuito**
⏱️ **Duración aproximada: 90 min + Q&A**
🤝 **Impulsado por InvokeApp para la comunidad PNM – Professional Network Madrid**

name: IA Workshop: Automatización para AEC con n8n: de la obra a los datos
description:
Este próximo **miércoles día 16 de marzo de 2026** (7PM hora de Madrid) tenemos nueva reunión del BIM Technology User Group, una reunión en la que realizaremos un **Workshop gratuito bajo el título de *[Automatización para AEC con n8n: de la obra a los datos](https://butic.es/automatizacion-n8n-datos-obra/)*.**

Correrá a cargo de **David Moreira**, Arquitecto especializado en transformación digital y automatización de procesos.

En el día a día de un proyecto AECO se generan constantemente **nuevos datos**: incidencias BIM, fotografías de obra, informes, actas, aprobaciones, cambios, avisos y tareas. El reto no está tanto en disponer de esa información como en **conseguir que llegue, en el momento adecuado**, a quien tiene que actuar sobre ella.
En este workshop online veremos cómo transformar ese problema en un flujo de trabajo automatizado utilizando **n8n**, una plataforma que permite conectar aplicaciones y automatizar procesos. A través de un caso práctico, construiremos paso a paso un flujo sencillo para entender qué ocurre desde que se genera un dato hasta que se convierte en una acción dentro del equipo.
Más que aprender a utilizar todas las posibilidades de n8n, la sesión busca comprender una metodología aplicable a muchos otros procesos: capturar información, estructurarla, analizarla, establecer prioridades y desencadenar respuestas de forma automática y trazable.
El propósito es descubrir **qué procesos merece la pena automatizar y por qué**, reduciendo tareas repetitivas y mejorando la circulación de información entre la oficina, la obra y los distintos agentes del proyecto. Una aproximación práctica a la automatización que permite empezar a construir soluciones útiles sin necesidad de ser especialista en programación.

El registro para acceder en directo vía Zoom, es éste: [https://butic.es/automatizacion-n8n-datos-obra/](https://butic.es/automatizacion-n8n-datos-obra/)

**¿Qué aprenderemos con David?**

1. Una forma clara de leer procesos AEC como flujos de información
2. Criterios para identificar tareas que pueden automatizarse
3. Una referencia concreta sobre cómo integrar n8n e IA manteniendo el control profesional

* ​Cómo funciona la lógica básica de n8n: entradas, nodos, datos, condiciones y ejecuciones.
* ​Cómo conectar una entrada de información con reglas de decisión, notificaciones y registros.
* ​Cómo transformar tareas repetitivas en flujos trazables sin perder criterio humano.
* ​Cómo identificar oportunidades de automatización en contextos AEC.
* ​Qué casos conviene automatizar, cuáles no, y cómo evitar agregar ruido innecesario al equipo.
* ​Cómo una capa de IA puede apoyar el resumen y priorización de información sin reemplazar la revisión profesional.

El registro para acceder en directo vía Zoom a esta primera Open BIM Class, es éste: [https://butic.es/automatizacion-n8n-datos-obra/](https://butic.es/automatizacion-n8n-datos-obra/)

name: Closing the Continuous Learning Loop: From Agent Traces to Agent Training
description:
**Zoom link**: [https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562](https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562)

**Talk #0: Introductions and Meetup Updates**
by Chris Fregly and Antje Barth

**Talk #1: Closing the Continuous Learning Loop: From Agent Traces to Agent Training**
by Rustem Feyzkhanov, Engineering Manager @ Snorkel.ai

name: Sept 24 - AI, ML and Computer Vision Meetup
description:
Join our virtual meetup on September 24 to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics across AI, ML, and computer vision.

**Date, Time and Location**

Sep 24, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/ai-ml-and-computer-vision-meetup-september-24-2026)**

**How Do Mercedes-Benz AI Principles Drive our Innovation?**

At Mercedes-Benz, our AI Principles guide every step of innovation, emphasizing responsible use, safety and reliability, explainability, and the protection of privacy. These principles go beyond statements and actively shape how we design, test, and deploy AI systems in real-world automotive and enterprise settings. In this talk, I will present how these principles inspired our recent research on when reusing LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) is effective. By combining theoretical analysis with synthetic data as a proxy for enterprise scenarios, we uncovered the strengths and limitations of modular AI components under constrained data access. Our findings provide practical guidance on when reused LoRAs could deliver high-quality results.

*About the Speaker*

[Mei-Yen Chen](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mei-yen-chen-22937787) is a Senior Data Scientist at Mercedes-Benz Tech Innovation GmbH in Germany with 10 years of industry experience in AI and data solutions. She leads early-stage AI projects across business functions and collaborates with research institutions on machine learning and responsible AI.

**Region Tokens as the Visual Primitive: From Recognition to World Modeling**

Patch-based tokenization has become the default interface between vision encoders and downstream models, yet patches carry no semantic structure and scale poorly with resolution and temporal extent. This talk presents a research program centered on replacing patch tokens with region-level representations — semantically dense tokens grounded in visual entities rather than arbitrary grid crops.

I will describe RELOCATE, REN, and T-REN, a progression of methods that produce region tokens via pooling, train them with region-level objectives, and extend them to video with temporal coherence. I will then present ongoing work integrating region tokens into VLMs to directly expand visual context capacity, and preliminary results on future region trajectory prediction as a foundation for world modeling.

The broader thesis is that region-level tokens are a more natural unit of visual computation than patches, and their advantage compounds as task complexity, resolution, and temporal horizon increase.

*About the Speaker*

[Savya Khosla](https://www.linkedin.com/in/savyakhosla/) is a second-year Ph.D. student at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, advised by Prof. Derek Hoiem and Prof. Alex Schwing.

**Leveraging Text-To-Image Diffusion Models for Consistent Set-to-Set Generation**

Image collections are humans' primary way of capturing the world, yet advances in generative editing remain largely inapplicable to this modality. We address this gap by introducing Match-and-Fuse - a zero-shot, training-free method for consistent set-to-set generation from image collections that share a common visual element but differ in viewpoint, capture time, and surrounding content.
Our key idea is a unified graph-based framework that combines dense correspondences with an emergent prior in text-to-image diffusion models to generate coherent canvases. We achieve state-of-the-art consistency and visual quality, and unlock new creative capabilities for content generation.

*About the Speaker*

[Kate Feingold](https://www.linkedin.com/in/katefeingold/) is a PhD student in Computer Vision at the Weizmann Institute of Science. Her research sits at the intersection of generative models, 3D/4D perception, and multimodal learning, focusing on problems where vision meets other modalities or paradigms in creative tasks.

**Yield Estimation of a Coffee in a dense environment**

This presentation provides a detailed workflow related to coffee yield estimation in a dense environment. With photos of pre-harvest coffee plants from a couple of coffee estates, details related to pre-processing, annotation to detect regions of interest (ROI), object detection training and inferencing results with various Yolo models and finally segmentation with SAM2 and Yolo\*-seg with training and inference results to determine the count of raw, pre-mature, mature and over-mature coffee berries and finally the yield of the entire estate. All this is based on real world data captured on iPhone and android phones.

*About the Speaker*

[Raghu M. Rao](http://www.linkedin.com/in/raghumrao) is a consultant working on applications of computer vision AI models. He was previously with AMD and Xilinx. He has a Ph.D. in Wireless Communications from UCLA and is a Senior Member, IEEE. His current interests are in applications of AI for agriculture, health care and wireless communications.

Stop doing this manually.
In this workshop, you'll customize and deploy a working AI research agent in 3 hours. Fork an existing competitive intelligence agent, wire in your own data sources (RSS feeds, APIs, whatever's available), and run it. Feed it a company or industry keyword. Get back structured intelligence: recent news, hiring patterns, market positioning, gaps, red flags.
**What you'll actually do:**

* Clone a working competitive intelligence agent from GitHub
* Add your own custom data sources (RSS feeds, open APIs, etc.)
* Test it live on a real company or competitor
* Walk away with a deployed agent you can run 100+ times

**Two use cases, one agent:**

1. **Job Seeker Mode** — Research a company before you apply, interview, or accept an offer. Understand growth, hiring, leadership, red flags.
2. **Competitive Mode** — Understand what competitors are doing, market gaps, hiring trends, strategic moves. For employees and side hustlers.

**What you need before the workshop:**

* 10 min of pre-work (optional, but recommended): Clone the GitHub repo, set up your API key, test it runs
* A laptop with a browser (Claude.ai)
* Basic comfort with Claude—you should already be asking it questions and iterating

**After the workshop:**

* Post-work recap doc: What you built, how to iterate, advanced techniques, troubleshooting
* Optional upsell: Advanced agent techniques course (separate paid offering)

**This is NOT:**

* A tutorial on "how to use AI"

name: Sept 17 - ADAS, AV, and AI Meetup
description:
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics across AI, ML, and computer vision.

**Time, Date and Location**

Sep 17, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/adas-av-and-ai-meetup-september-17-2026)**

**AI for Autonomous Driving: From Data to Decisions**

Building reliable automated driving systems is as much a data and engineering challenge as a modeling one. In this talk, Tin will share perspectives from his work at Porsche AG on applying modern AI methods across the autonomous driving development process, from making sense of large-scale driving data to understanding and evaluating how AI-based systems behave on the road. He'll discuss lessons learned from real-world development, where today's approaches shine, and where hard problems remain for the ADAS and AV community.

*About the Speaker*

[Tin Stribor Sohn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/tin-stribor-sohn/) is a PhD Student at Porsche AG and Karlsruhe Institute of Technology in the area of Foundation Models for Scenario Understanding and Decision Making in Autonomous Robotics, Tech Lead at Data Driven Engineering for Autonomous Driving, Prior: Master in CS at University of Tuebingen with focus on Computer Vision and Deep Learning and co-founder of a software company for smart EV charging

**Advancing ADAS and Autonomous Vehicle Development with Multimodal Data**

ADAS and autonomous vehicle systems rely on increasingly complex data from cameras, video, LiDAR, radar, and other sensor streams. In this session, Murilo will introduce Voxel51 and explore how the latest multimodal capabilities in FiftyOne help teams bring these data sources together to better understand their datasets and model behavior. He’ll discuss how unified workflows for visualization, search, curation, and evaluation can help ADAS and AV teams uncover challenging scenarios, investigate model failures, and build safer, more reliable autonomous systems.

*About the Speaker*

[Murilo Gustineli](https://www.linkedin.com/in/murilo-gustineli/) is a Machine Learning Engineer at Voxel51 working at the intersection of representation learning and computer vision. He holds an M.S. in Computer Science from Georgia Tech, where he co-leads the DS@GT Applied Research & Competitions group, advancing machine learning research through competitive challenges and peer-reviewed publications.

**From Survey-Grade Maps to Physical AI: Scaling Real-World Data for Training and Simulation**

Physical AI systems are increasingly constrained not by model architectures, but by the availability of scalable, high-fidelity real-world data. This talk explores how Dynamic Map Platform transforms survey-grade road assets collected across 1.8 million km of roads worldwide into training- and simulation-ready datasets, including point clouds, imagery, HD maps, road surface models, and 3D Gaussian Splatting representations.

We will discuss why geometric accuracy, semantic understanding, and real-world diversity are critical to building robust autonomous driving systems. Attendees will learn how real-world geospatial data can be structured and scaled for AI training and simulation workflows.

*About the Speaker*

[Ryoto Miyake](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ryoto-miyake/) is a Software Engineer at Dynamic Map Platform, where he works on transforming large-scale geospatial data into AI-ready datasets for training, simulation, and validation, such as HD maps and 3D Gaussian Splatting. With a background in transportation engineering, he works closely with automotive manufacturers and industry partners to bridge large-scale real-world mapping data with next-generation AI and mobility systems.

name: Sept 30 - Building Composable Vision Workflows in FiftyOne
description:
This workshop explores the [FiftyOne](https://docs.voxel51.com/index.html) plugin framework to build custom computer vision applications. You’ll learn to extend the FiftyOne App with Python based panels and server side operators, as well as integrate external tools for labeling, vector search, and model inference into your dataset views.

**Date, Time and Location**

Sep 30, 2026
9 AM - 10 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/building-composable-vision-workflows-in-fiftyone-september-30-2026)**

You’ll also automate repetitive tasks by writing custom workflows executing within the FiftyOne environment. Attendees will learn to transform FiftyOne from a visualization tool into a central hub for your vision stack.

What you'll learn:

* **Build Python plugins.** Define plugin manifests and directory structures to register custom functionality within the FiftyOne ecosystem.
* **Develop server side operators.** Write functions to execute model inference, data cleaning, or metadata updates from the App interface.
* **Build interactive panels.** Create custom UI dashboards using to visualize model metrics or specialized dataset distributions.
* **Manage operator execution contexts.** Pass data between the App front end and your backend to build dynamic user workflows.
* **Implement delegated execution.** Configure background workers to handle long running data processing tasks without blocking the user interface.
* **Build labeling integrations.** Streamline the flow of data between FiftyOne and annotation platforms through custom triggers and ingestion scripts.
* **Extend vector database support.** Program custom connectors for external vector stores to enable semantic search across large sample datasets.
* **Package and share plugins.** Distribute your extensions internally and externally

name: Open Source Climate Accounting: What Exists, What's Missing+Where To Contribute
description:
Climate accounting increasingly depends on systems that were never designed to work together. Registries use different standards and data models. The same activity can appear across multiple systems. Measurement data may come from sensors, satellite observations, models, or manual reporting, often with limited provenance or no straightforward way for downstream users to verify how a claim was produced.

These are not only reporting problems but they are problems of interoperability, provenance, reconciliation and trust between independent systems.

A substantial amount of open-source work already exists to address them, but much of it remains fragmented or little known outside the communities that built it. This session will map that landscape: what is already available, what is mature enough to use today, what remains experimental and where meaningful technical contributions are still needed.

The aim is not to argue that blockchain is the answer to climate accounting. It is to look practically at where distributed ledgers, verifiable data, open standards and other open-source infrastructure can solve specific problems or where they cannot.

Structure - The session would begin with a short framing of the technical problems behind climate and impact accounting: provenance, reconciliation, double counting, interoperability and verification across organisational boundaries.

From there, members of the LF Decentralized Trust community could walk through existing open-source projects and frameworks, explaining what they were built to solve, how mature they are and where they are being used today.

The final part would focus on the gaps: problems that remain unsolved, areas where maintainers would welcome contributions and practical ways for developers, researchers and organisations to get involved.

The IEEE ClimateChain Global Hackathon ([https://ieee-climatechain-hack.devpost.com/](https://ieee-climatechain-hack.devpost.com/)) would be introduced as one of those routes to contribution.

The goal is for participants to leave with a clearer picture of what already exists, which problems are genuinely open and where their time and technical skills could have the greatest value.

**Zoom Meeting Link**: [https://zoom.us/my/hyperledger.community.3?pwd=UE90WHhEaHRqOGEyMkV3cldKa2d2dz09](https://zoom.us/my/hyperledger.community.3?pwd=UE90WHhEaHRqOGEyMkV3cldKa2d2dz09)

name: Tras la Máscara de Async Rust
description:
Después de un tiempo de inactividad volvemos a la carga con otra sesión de [Herme García](https://github.com/hermeGarcia).

**¿Qué sucede realmente por debajo de \`async/await\` en Rust?**

En esta charla vamos a explorar cómo Rust construye su modelo de computación asíncrona combinando piezas fundamentales del lenguaje. Veremos cómo Rust **se apoya en su sistema de tipos y el ownership model** para ejecutar trabajo de forma asíncrona. Partiendo de estos fundamentos, iremos construyendo una intuición de **cómo funciona un executor** y cómo estas mismas piezas **permiten llegar a un runtime completo como Tokio**.

*El evento tiene espíritu inclusivo y de respeto, todos son bienvenidos. Este evento se organiza bajo el paraguas del [código de conducta de la comunidad de Rust](https://rust-lang.org/es/policies/code-of-conduct/).*
